test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 15 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper sells wheat at Rs. 20/kg that he purchased at Rs. 18/kg and he gives only 900 gm of wheat instead of 1 kg while selling. The actual percentage profit of the shopkeeper is:
solution:
**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 18/kg, Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 20/kg, Amount sold = 900 gm = 0.9 kg

**Formula:**

Profit = SP - CP

Profit% = (({Profit} / {CP}) times 100)

**Calculation:**

Cost for 900 gm

⇒ (CP_{900gm} = 18 × 0.9 = Rs. 16.2)

Profit ⇒ (20 - 16.2 = Rs. 3.8)

Profit Percentage ⇒ ((3.8 / 16.2) \times 100) ⇒ 23.456

**⇒ Approx. 23.45%**
